searchText: okay i traced down the weirdest bug ever... when i set `export DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS="0x6f22fFbC56eFF051aECF839396DD1eD9aD6BBA9D"` on the genesis tool, all the blocks built are missing (even for deneb, let alone peerdas). But when i remove it, it defaults to `DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS="0x424242..."` and then it works and produces blocks! is there some specific reason why one deposit contract works and the other fails? 😅 As far as i can tell, the genesis tool doesn't have any specific logic so any address should work, but it could ofc be our tool as well... Peerdas-devnet-4 is live! 😄 https://peerdas-devnet-4.ethpandaops.io/ We have dora running here: https://dora.peerdas-devnet-4.ethpandaops.io/ There are blobs and transactions being submitted to the network. Fulu went live just now and the network is stable so far. fingers crossed 🙂 for a couple of days atleast some findings 1. <@498331483732312075> i see a quick fork and recover are all node just fullnode? 2. same for nimbus geth 2 yeah thanks, looking into it i still haven't found any supernode on dora yet looking.... participation rate dropped is not a good sign <@199561711278227457> can I have grandine image update please? it contains some fixes from the scenario tests i think we don't have supernode peers, toggling the supernode peers in dora does nothing might slow down syncing significantly according to this diagram, alot of the peers are lonely custodians but if there are forks now, we are now sure no one reconstructed _incorrectly_ if clients can sync from this devnet, solely based on the sample size, their column sync mechanism is indeed very practical, rather not optimistic which branch or commit? everything should be a supernode :/ can you check the flags if the supernode flags have been properly set? it could ofc be thatthe dora view is wrong this commit `c4e3807`: https://github.com/hangleang/grandine/commit/c4e3807012b8922f20ec3d6eebdf418af1b54c0f The dora view is wrong. It's still using `csc` field from the ENR instead of `cgc`. But if you check the peer details, all peers report a `cgc=0x80 (128)`, which means that they should be supernodes. Thanks for the clarification 😀 phew, was afraid there was a misconfig 😄 gradine was just updated and teku-geth-3 might also need some love there are issues on Teku side, but I also see this a lot: ``` tech.pegasys.teku.ethereum.executionclient.response.InvalidRemoteResponseException: Invalid remote response from the execution client: TimeoutException ``` is there a way to open metrics, I forgot? grafana.observability.ethpandaops.io/ Does this work for you? Can you login? all good, thank you!

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
okay i traced down the weirdest bug ever...
when i set  `export DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS="0x6f22fFbC56eFF051aECF839396DD1eD9aD6BBA9D"` on the genesis tool, all the blocks built are missing (even for deneb, let alone peerdas). But when i remove it, it defaults to `DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS="0x424242..."` and then it works and produces blocks! is there some specific reason why one deposit contract works and the other fails? 😅  As far as i can tell, the genesis tool doesn't have any specific logic so any address should work, but it could ofc be our tool as well...
